cells.quote: An independent t test was run to compare the mean scores of the control and experimental groups on the grammar posttest. So the null hypothesis as the use of grammar consciousness-raising activities has no statistically significant effect on young EFL learners’ grammar performance was rejected. O.outcome_detail: understanding and correction of cosmological ideas

cells.quote: Therefore, within any G.C.S.E. course, we advise teachers to commence cosmology with a review of some of the observational evidence in favour of the evolutionary Big Bang model: the Hubble relation and the cosmic microwave background radiation.
cells.note: The authors make a narrative recommendation and predict that an observational approach will help address misconceptions; no comparative learning study is reported.

D.treatment: include nucleosynthesis with the Hubble relation and CMB

O.outcome_detail: strength of understanding of Big Bang theory

cells.quote: We advocate that teachers include nucleosynthesis in any advanced level course as, taken in combination with the Hubble relation and the cosmic microwave background radiation, they make the Big Bang theory appear highly watertight.
cells.note: This is an instructional recommendation, not an experimental comparison.

D.treatment: teach astrophysics in the middle of the physics course
D.comparison: teach astrophysics as the last subject

cells.quote: Astrophysics as a discrete unit of teaching typically comes last within any G.C.S.E. or A-level scheme of work. Since the topic requires a synthesis of prior knowledge from many parts of a syllabus, this is of little surprise. The downside is, of course, that teaching astrophysics as the last subject will probably not leave sufficient time for it. Attempting to teach this topic earlier, say at the beginning of the final year of a course, may prove productive, especially given its timeless popularity.
cells.note: The study argues that moving astrophysics earlier may preserve teaching time; it reports no measured outcome.

O.outcome_detail: sense of Universal size and coherent cosmology sequence

cells.quote: Within astrophysics, cosmology nearly always comes last. The reason for this primarily appears that astrophysics is taught lengthwise as a bottom-up subject: starting off with Earth-bound phenomena and working up in scale through the Solar System to the Universe as a whole. The bottom-up method is, however, a sound premise because it institutes in pupils a sense of Universal size.
cells.note: The authors recommend cosmology as the final astrophysics topic based on a bottom-up progression; no comparative study is reported.
